text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party government is under serious threat after opposition parties join forces to present united front.
- Many Albanians want to end their contract with the largest of all the pyramid/investment schemes, Vefa Holding, but the Tirana courts are turning down their requests.
- Police broke up a protest rally organised by some small right-wing parties and a group of former political dissidents.
- Inter-parliamentary Union committee asked Berisha for the unconditional release of the jailed opposition Socialist leader, Fatos Nano.
- Opposition parties plan to hold a demonstration on Sunday in the western city of Durres to support people who have lost their savings in the failed pyramid schemes.
- A man in eastern Albania kills himself after losing eight million leks deposited at one of the pyramid schemes. The money was sent to him by his two sons working in Greece.
- More than 200 protestors have been arrested in three cities after last weekend's demonstrations.
- Parliament passed a law late last night concerning compensation for the investors of failed pyramid schemes.
- The lek continues to fall, now quoted at 126 per dollar.
- Rrapush Xhaferri, the arrested chief manager of a pyramid scheme, in a call from prison, promised to give depositors their cash back.
- U.S. State Department reports on Albanian elections, freedom of press, judicial system, respect of the human rights and minorities.
- Depositors in southern towns of Gjirokaster and Tepelene held a demonstration over the failed pyramid schemes.
